:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Suppose $|\,\mathbf{a}\,|=13$ and the angle between vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is $\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}.$ Find the scalar projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =|\,a\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =13\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) \\  & =13\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{13}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Let $\mathbf{a}=\langle 3,3,-1 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 2,-7,0 \rangle.$ Find the scalar projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 2+3\cdot (-7)+(-1)\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-7)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{15}{\sqrt{53}}.\end{aligned}
$$
